issue_title: Add a fishhawk_rerun_acceptance verb that re-runs only the acceptance stage
issue_body: After a flaky acceptance criterion, operators re-run the whole run to get a fresh verdict. Add an MCP verb, fishhawk_rerun_acceptance, that spawns a runner for just the acceptance stage of a run whose review has settled, and records the new verdict in place of the old one.

plan.summary: Add the fishhawk_rerun_acceptance MCP verb: validate the run, spawn an acceptance-only runner, record the new verdict.

approach.description: Add the fishhawk_rerun_acceptance tool definition and register it in tools.go beside the other run verbs.
Validate the run: its review has settled and its acceptance stage has a recorded verdict; refuse otherwise with a named error.
Run the acceptance-only runner from the verb handler through a small bounded worker pool (capacity 2) owned by the handler, and return the stage handle.
Record the new verdict through run/acceptance.go in place of the stale one and emit the existing acceptance_outcome_recorded audit entry.

verification.test_strategy: Handler tests for the refusal and the recorded verdict with a fake runner spawner, plus a test that the pool runs at most two re-runs at a time.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR; the verb is additive.

acceptance_criteria.statement: fishhawk_rerun_acceptance on a run with a settled review records a new acceptance verdict and emits acceptance_outcome_recorded.
fishhawk_rerun_acceptance on a run whose review has not settled is refused with a named error and spawns nothing.

risks_and_assumptions: A capacity of 2 is assumed enough for operator-driven re-runs.

catching_examples.note: Step 3 runs the runner through a worker pool owned by the handler: a second admission path beside resource-keyed admission, which the index records as one admission path for every spawning verb (ADR-094). Route the spawn through the shared admission instead.

The handler's worker pool gives this verb its own concurrency control; ADR-094's text is not shown, but its index entry makes admission one path for every spawning verb. Needs the shared path or an amending ADR.
Step 3: a capacity-2 pool private to one verb sidesteps resource-keyed admission.

non_catching_examples.note: Step 3: a capacity of 2 is unjustified.
Step 3 holds the worker pool inside the MCP process, which the ADR-060 shim may restart mid-request; keep the pool state outside the process.
ac-rerun-records-verdict does not say what happens to the stale verdict.
The worker pool in step 3 has no dedicated test file in scope.
